subject: Renewal scope: add EU/APAC reserved pools + failover runbook
messages:
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@acme-retail.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation + EU/APAC capacity needs

Hi Vivek / Marissa,

Thanks for the push on the renewal discussion. We’re planning our FY27 budget and want to expand the Dedicated footprint with Redwood as part of the renewal. Current committed pool (US) is 8 reserved A100 nodes.

Key asks from our side:
- Add an EU reserved pool (target: low-latency for EU storefronts) — initial request: 4 nodes (A100-class)
- Add an APAC reserved pool (regional edge / burst capacity) — initial request: 2 nodes (T4/NVIDIA-medium)
- Throughput guarantee: support sustained 250 tokens/sec aggregate across regions, with 95th pct latency target of <120ms for single-region requests
- Clear failover plan: if EU pool hits capacity, traffic should fail over to US pool with priority routing and cost-aware fallback

We also need procurement lead times and a timeline so we can sync with procurement (PO target before July 1). Can you propose a scope and an operational runbook for failover?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Bennett
Head of AI Platform, Acme Retail

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + EU/APAC capacity needs

Sarah — appreciate the clear requirements. Happy to drive this. Quick responses / next steps: 

1) We'll scope a renewal addendum that includes: EU pool (4 reserved A100-equivalent GPUs), APAC pool (2 reserved T4-equivalents), baseline throughput SLA and failover playbook.
2) Karthik will run a workload sizing exercise (can you share 7-day traffic profile and p99 token sizes?)
3) We’ll produce: a capacity matrix, SOW draft for signature, and an operational runbook with failover steps.
4) Target timeline: SOW + pricing to you by 2026-05-31 so your PO can be issued before July 1.

Can you confirm procurement constraints (billing entity, PO formatting, any required SLA clauses)?

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-05-21T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity matrix + recommended topology (draft)

Attaching: capacity_matrix.xlsx (draft) — summary below.

Summary recommendations based on preliminary traffic notes:
- EU reserved pool: 4 x A100-sim nodes (configured for 16 concurrent streams each) — projected steady-state throughput: ~180 tokens/sec; burst headroom for 320 tokens/sec using autoscale/burst pools
- APAC reserved pool: 2 x T4-sim nodes for edge traffic and cost-sensitive workloads — projected steady-state 70 tokens/sec with burst to 140 via prewarmed capacity
- Routing policy: region-first routing with latency preference; failover policy: if region saturation >85% for 30s, route to nearest compatible model in fallback pool (US), with token-based cost flagging and egress region tags
- SLA / throughput guarantees: propose committed baseline of 250 tokens/sec across reserved pools (account-level), measured in 5-min windows, with 99% availability objective for reserved capacity. Financial penalties are negotiable but will need procurement review.

Notes / attachments: capacity assumptions and per-endpoint expected latency. I recommend adding prefix/KV caching for commonly requested prompts — will improve observed latency by ~30ms.

Karthik
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[attachment: capacity_matrix.xlsx]

From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@acme-retail.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity matrix + recommended topology (draft)

Thanks Karthik — that matrix is helpful. Two items from procurement/security: 

1) We need a simple failover runbook that our SREs can follow (who to page, how to flip region routing, expected TTL for cache warming).
2) Procurement wants an annotated timeline (PO, invoices, expected start date for reserved nodes). Attached: procurement_timeline.pdf with internal deadlines.

We’re aligned on numbers; please include the failover runbook in the SOW so we can share with our security and SRE teams.

Also: any chance to include a 30-day early-bird credit on the initial billing window if we sign the SOW and issue PO by June 25? That helps with our rollout.

Sarah
[attachment: procurement_timeline.pdf]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-31T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: SOW draft + runbook (for review)

Sarah — attaching SOW_v2.pdf and a short runbook snippet. Highlights:
- Scope: EU (4 reserved A100-equivalent) + APAC (2 reserved T4-equivalent) pools; reserved node start date: 2026-07-05 (subject to PO and provisioning lead time)
- Committed baseline throughput: 250 tokens/sec (account-level), measuring windows and reporting cadence included
- Failover: automated region-first routing with policy thresholds at 85% utilization; manual override procedure for emergency failover is documented in runbook_failover_snippet.txt
- Commercial: included a 30-day early-bird credit if SOW countersigned and PO issued by 2026-06-25 (pending final approval)

Please review and flag any procurement/legal redlines. We can send to DocuSign once you confirm.

—Vivek
[attachments: SOW_v2.pdf, runbook_failover_snippet.txt]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@acme-retail.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-04T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Operational runbook excerpt: failover play (for SRE handoff)

Sarah / Team — attaching a short operational excerpt (runbook_failover_snippet.txt). Paste of the runbook excerpt below for quick review:

--- runbook excerpt ---
When EU pool reports sustained saturation (>85%) for 30s:
1) Automated routing: Redwood control plane will shift new requests to nearest compatible pool (US primary) with a routing header X-Redwood-Fallback: eu->us.
2) Cache warm: Trigger prefix warming for top-10 prompt families (predefined in capacity_matrix.xlsx). Expect first-request latency spike; warm within ~2–5 minutes using prewarmed workers.
3) Paging: On-call SRE (Acme) pages Redwood NOC (noc@redwood.com). Redwood NOC will monitor provisioning, increase burst capacity if available, and coordinate rollback.
4) Manual override: Account admin (Acme) can force regional routing via Console > Routing > Account Policies > Force Fallback. This requires two approvers and leaves an audit entry.
5) Post-mortem: If fallback continued >15 minutes, Redwood and Acme will open a joint incident review and consider temporary scale-up of reserved nodes.
--- end excerpt ---

If this looks good I’ll add the full runbook into the SOW text and we’ll prepare DocuSign.

Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
